research: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/speech-generation: the prebuilt voice list with one-word characters (Charon informative, Iapetus clear, Rasalgethi informative, Schedar even, Sadaltager knowledgeable, Orus firm, Fenrir excitable, Achird friendly, Umbriel easy-going, Enceladus breathy, Zubenelgenubi casual); long director's notes cause voice drift, so keep style short; pick the voice first, then a short style; capitals for emphasis
https://dev.to/googleai/how-to-prompt-gemini-31s-new-text-to-speech-model-24bb: name a specific place for an accent ('as heard in Croydon') rather than just 'British'
https://replicate.com/google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts/readme: style prompt, text and tags must all point the same way, or the voice sounds off
https://livekit.com/blog/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-prompting-guide: extra punctuation to steer pace no longer works on 3.1 Flash TTS; say the pace in words
https://simonwillison.net/2026/Apr/15/gemini-31-flash-tts/: plain regional prompts (Newcastle, Exeter) are understood; the place name does the work

options.idea: Home Counties, privately educated Tory minister, mid-fifties, media-trained and smooth; Charon's informative, measured weight sounds like a man used to being listened to, not a caricature.
options.note:
Accent: Home Counties, privately educated, upper-middle class; light and natural, a real MP, nothing plummy or put on.
Style: Minister in his fifties, back of his car, irritated, telling his aide on the phone he'd been perfectly clear.
Pace: Brisk, clipped, impatient.

options.idea: Edinburgh professional class, a former advocate turned minister, late forties to fifty; Iapetus's clear, precise tone gives a cool, lawyerly exasperation rather than bluster.
options.note:
Accent: Edinburgh, professional middle class, ex-lawyer; soft and everyday, not broad, not exaggerated.
Style: Minister around fifty, distracted in his car, correcting his aide on the phone, more weary than angry.
Pace: Even, precise, a tired sigh in it.

options.idea: Self-made Cheshire businessman turned minister, late fifties, grammar school, accent sanded down by years in Westminster; Orus's firm, heavier voice gives a bossy, used-to-getting-his-way older man.
options.note:
Accent: Cheshire, grammar school, wealthy now; years in Westminster have smoothed it, light and ordinary, not stagey.
Style: Minister late fifties, a businessman at heart, snapping at an aide on the phone like a junior employee.
Pace: Firm, quick, slightly raised.

notes: Line to render as one take: "I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!" No muffling in the note; that is added in the edit. All three avoid South London, Leeds and Liverpool so the minister never shares a region with the crew. Option c's Cheshire is northern-adjacent to Liverpool; if it reads too close to the Liverpool paramedic, a and b are the safer contrast.
